findings.title: Confidence-tiering is claim-shape-gated, not a blanket rule
findings.principle: Every load-bearing claim in a final reply (a state-of-the-world statement the owner will act on: 'this works', 'this covers all 28 salons', 'this is safe to ship', 'this pattern affects N files') is tagged verified, expect, or assume before the reply ends. The tag is required regardless of whether the sentence happens to contain one of the specific trigger words (fixed/done/verified/confirmed/resolved) that today's gates scan for.
findings.why: Rule 15 defines the three-tier system (verified/expect/assume) but its trigger is narrow: 'a claim that can be checked against the live world', mainly versioned/external facts. The actual enforcement is five separate narrow regex gates, each covering one claim SHAPE: verify-before-done-gate only fires on the literal words fixed/done/fertig/erledigt/verified/confirmed/resolved/works now/passes; stat-source-gate only fires on persuasion-statistic shapes (n% of users, studies show, Nx more); paint-proof-gate only fires on visibility/occlusion claims about fixed/sticky/overlay elements; env-claim-needs-evidence-gate only fires on sandbox/permission-block claims; checkbox-evidence-gate only fires on a newly ticked `- [x]` line. A load-bearing claim outside these five shapes (e.g. 'this query is safe for concurrent bookings', 'the migration is backward compatible', 'this covers every route') carries no confidence tag requirement and no gate.
findings.local_evidence: verify-before-done-gate.py:40-44 CLAIM_RE is a fixed word list; stat-source-gate.py:29-38 STAT regex requires a specific %/x-multiplier/studies-show shape; paint-proof-gate.py:37-48 PAINT_CLAIM requires stays/never-moves/not-covered phrasing plus an overlay-subject noun. None of the five gates has a general 'unqualified assertion of fact' detector.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn "confidence" CLAUDE.md hooks/reality-check-gate.py hooks/stat-source-gate.py -> one hit, CLAUDE.md:77 ('mark it as low-confidence imitation'), scoped to rule 4 (imitation of a brand/library), not to general claims. grep -rn "tier every claim" ~/.claude -> only fable-execution/SKILL.md section 7 ('close' checklist, a one-time end-of-turn step, not a per-claim runtime gate).
findings.existing_coverage: partial: rule 15 sets the tier vocabulary (verified/expect/assume) and fable-execution step 7 repeats it at CLOSE time; five Stop gates each enforce ONE narrow claim shape. No gate or rule enforces the tier on an arbitrary load-bearing claim that doesn't match one of those five regex families.
findings.where_it_should_live: CLAUDE.md rule 15 (extend the trigger from 'checkable external fact' to 'any load-bearing state claim'), REPORT_SYSTEM.md section 4.3 (Verified)
findings.enforcement: gate: a generalized claim-confidence gate is hard to regex reliably (the five existing gates are narrow precisely because a broad claim-detector over-fires); more realistic is a REPORT_SYSTEM template requirement (the Verified section must tag EVERY bullet, not just ones a gate happened to catch) plus a periodic self-audit, not a new Stop gate

findings.title: No required content for an 'I could not verify this' answer
findings.principle: A reply that says a claim could not be verified must state, in the same sentence or the next one: what was tried, why it failed or was inconclusive, and the single concrete thing (a credential, a decision, a tool, a piece of data) that would unblock verification. 'Could not verify' with no attempt described is not an acceptable close.
findings.why: Without this, 'I couldn't verify X' is indistinguishable from 'I didn't try to verify X', and the owner has no way to tell laziness from a genuine external blocker, or to know what to hand back to unblock it. The estate already treats this exact failure mode as serious in the adjacent case of environment-permission claims (env-claim-needs-evidence-gate) and owner-facing setup punts (owner-punt-gate demands the agent try gh/MCP/env itself before punting) and root-cause-free deflection (no-defer-excuse-gate's ROOTCAUSE requirement) — but none of those three generalizes to the plain case of 'I could not verify this' about a fact, a number, or a behavior.
findings.local_evidence: REPORT_SYSTEM.md line 42-43: 'A claim without its evidence line reads as unverified and must be phrased as such' -- this mandates the LABEL ('unverified') but never mandates the CONTENT (what was tried / why it failed / what unblocks it). Compare owner-punt-gate.py lines 8-13 which DOES require the agent to have exhausted gh/MCP/env before punting a setup task to the owner -- the analogous discipline for a verification punt does not exist.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn "could not verify|couldn't verify|unable to verify|cannot verify" CLAUDE.md hooks/*.py REPORT_SYSTEM.md -> zero hits describing required content (one incidental hit, CLAUDE.md:363, about a hook's own limits, not about reply content).
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the LABEL is required (rule 15's assume/expect tier, REPORT_SYSTEM 4.3); the CONTENT of a failed-verification statement is not specified anywhere
findings.where_it_should_live: REPORT_SYSTEM.md section 4.3 (Verified), as a sibling rule to the existing evidence-line requirement
findings.enforcement: checklist item in REPORT_SYSTEM template; could be gated the same way owner-punt-gate is (regex for a verification-failure phrase co-occurring with no attempt/reason/unblocker language) but a first pass as behavioral law is the right size at 28-salon scale

findings.title: Self-produced numbers cite the result, not the reproducible method
findings.principle: Any count, measurement, or size the assistant produces itself (a grep count, a getBoundingClientRect value, a pixel-sampled color, a route/file tally) is reported with the exact command or script that produced it, not just the resulting number, so the owner or a later session can rerun the identical check and get the identical number.
findings.why: A 'measured: X' note that omits the method is unfalsifiable after the fact -- if the number is later disputed or drifts, nobody (not even the same agent next session, per rule 19's re-verify-after-compaction law) can tell whether the original measurement was even correct, only whether it was CLAIMED. This is the self-produced-number analogue of rule 15's already-strict handling of external statistics (stat-source-gate demands a named source for a recalled stat); the estate never extended that discipline to numbers it computes itself.
findings.local_evidence: In the live repo: _plans/PDP_CONSISTENCY.md:27 'Frost measured: at scroll 0 the bar is rgba(255,255,255,0) with blur(0px); scrolled past the hero it is rgba(255,255,255,0.8) with blur(4px)' -- states the values, never the script/selector used to read them. _plans/SEARCH_MAP_OVERHAUL.md:56 'cards 245.33x163.55 (1.5005 = 3:2), heart 44x44' -- same pattern, no getBoundingClientRect call or Playwright selector shown. _plans/WORKLOG.md:13 'measured: PermissionError' cites the error class but not the exact probe command run to trigger it.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn "reproducible|re-run|rerun the|exact grep|cite the command|show the command" CLAUDE.md REPORT_SYSTEM.md hooks/*.py -> zero hits requiring the method to be shown alongside a self-produced number.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: REPORT_SYSTEM 4.3 requires 'HOW' a claim was proven (test output, screenshot, curl, gate PASS, measured number) but 'measured number' is accepted as HOW by itself -- the number stands in for its own proof, which is the exact gap.
findings.where_it_should_live: REPORT_SYSTEM.md section 4.3, and the '`measured:`' convention referenced across the design-system docs
findings.enforcement: checklist: a 'measured:' line must carry either the literal command/selector or a `file:line` to a script that computed it, mirroring checkbox-evidence-gate's existing acceptance of file:line/verified:/measured: markers -- that gate already half-solves this by requiring a marker, it just doesn't require the marker's PAYLOAD to be reproducible

findings.title: The only enforcement against burying the lede was killed and never replaced
findings.principle: When a Stop-gate enforcement mechanism is neutered because its FAILURE MODE (forcing a full re-send that repeats the whole reply) is worse than the problem it solves, the underlying principle gets a non-blocking replacement in the same change, not silence. For 'lead with the answer, don't bury it under structure': append a short correction rather than block-and-resend, or move the check earlier (PreToolUse / draft stage) instead of at Stop.
findings.why: Rule 2 ('lead with a recommendation'), REPORT_SYSTEM 4.1 ('outcome first line'), and feedback_recommend_and_visualize.md are all now enforced by exactly nothing live. The 2026-07-21 neutering decision correctly diagnosed that blocking-and-forcing-a-resend was the wrong mechanism, but the fix removed the mechanism instead of finding a better one, so the actual owner complaint this was built for ('why did u put so much text', 'you need to give me recommendations, I want you to think') now has zero live backstop -- it is pure behavioral discipline, the exact failure category rule 25 in FABLE_DNA and memory feedback_rules_are_hooks both say does not hold under task-focus pressure.
findings.local_evidence: hooks/concise-response-gate.py line 26: `sys.exit(0)  # NEUTERED 2026-07-21 (owner order) , see docstring` -- every line of logic below is dead code. hooks/always-recommend-gate.py line 24: identical pattern, `sys.exit(0)  # NEUTERED 2026-07-21 (owner order)`. memory/feedback_no_reply_blocking_gates.md confirms this was a deliberate owner order and explicitly says 'the neutering IS the owner's decision' and forbids re-enabling them as-is.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n "sys.exit(0)" hooks/concise-response-gate.py hooks/always-recommend-gate.py -> both return before their detection logic runs, confirmed by direct read of both files. No other hook in the 134-file listing targets 'leads with the answer' / 'buries the recommendation' as its trigger.
findings.existing_coverage: none live; the rule text survives in CLAUDE.md rules 2/8 and two memory files, with zero runtime check
findings.where_it_should_live: a new lightweight mechanism, e.g. an append-only PostToolUse-timed nudge before the reply is finalized (not a Stop-gate re-send), or a PreToolUse check on the draft before it's sent
findings.enforcement: gate:non-blocking-lede-check -- fires before the message is sent (not after, to avoid the resend problem), appends a short 'lede is buried, move the answer to sentence 1' note the model can act on without re-sending a rejected reply; needs its own adversarial test pass (rule 12.5) given the prior mechanism's failure mode

findings.title: No rule for when a change must be shown as a diff versus described in prose
findings.principle: A non-visual code change (a logic tweak, a threshold, a query, a copy string) that is small enough to show (roughly under 15 changed lines) is pasted as a diff or before/after snippet in the summary; larger or purely structural changes are described in prose naming the structural delta. Mockups already get an equivalent rule (mockup-first pipeline shows the actual rendered page); ordinary code edits have no equivalent for TEXT.
findings.why: REPORT_SYSTEM 4.2 requires listing every touched file with one line of WHY, but 'why' answers intent, not WHAT changed. For a one-line threshold or copy change, prose description ('tightened the retry window') can silently diverge from what was actually typed, and the owner has no cheap way to catch it without opening the file themselves -- which defeats the point of a phone-readable summary. Visual changes get exactly this discipline already (mockup-first: 'a copy of the real page... show before/after').
findings.local_evidence: CLAUDE.md 'Surgical edits only' rule 5 says 'git diff after each fix, verify only the intended thing changed' -- this is the AGENT'S OWN self-check, not a requirement to show that diff to the owner in the summary.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn "show.*diff|git diff after|paste the diff" CLAUDE.md REPORT_SYSTEM.md -> only the self-check line above; nothing requiring the diff to appear in the owner-facing report.
findings.existing_coverage: none for text/code changes; full coverage exists for the visual case (mockup-first law)
findings.where_it_should_live: REPORT_SYSTEM.md section 4.2 (Files), as a size-gated addendum
findings.enforcement: checklist rule; a line-count threshold makes it mechanically checkable in review but is not worth a Stop gate at 28-salon scale -- becomes worth gating once the team crosses roughly 3+ people relying on the summary alone to sign off on backend changes without reading the diff themselves

findings.title: No rule for correcting the owner on a wrong external fact (distinct from a code/reality contradiction)
findings.principle: When the owner states a checkable external fact that is wrong (a library's behavior, a payment provider's policy, a legal requirement, a pricing threshold) and it is load-bearing for the task, state the correction plainly with the source in the same turn, before proceeding on the owner's version. This is distinct from rule 18 (which covers the codebase or memory contradicting a stated premise about THIS estate) and distinct from rule 3 (which covers disagreeing with a proposed COURSE OF ACTION, not a factual claim).
findings.why: Rule 18 is scoped to 'the code or reality contradicts what the prompt asserted' -- its own examples are both about the estate's own state ('the X gate blocks Y', 'we already have Z'), not about an external fact like a Stripe rule or a Swiss regulatory threshold. Rule 3 is scoped to disagreeing with a SUGGESTION, and its own worked phrasing is about a plan's failure mode, not about a factual error. A gap exists in between: the owner asserting something false about the outside world that the assistant can check (rule 15's exact 'external, versioned, drifts' territory) but that no rule obligates CORRECTING once found wrong, only verifying.
findings.local_evidence: The Stripe integration is live in this codebase (TWINT/discount/credits per project_money_features_shipped.md) and pricing/VAT decisions are deferred (project_commission_vat_deferred.md) -- exactly the kind of external-policy claim where a wrong owner assumption ('Stripe doesn't support X', 'VAT applies at Y threshold') would be load-bearing and is not covered by rule 18's contradiction-surfacing wording.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn "factually wrong|owner is wrong|user is wrong|correct the owner" CLAUDE.md -> zero hits. Rule 18's own text (read in full) uses only 'the code or reality contradicts' and 'the user saying X does not make it so' -- both anchored to THIS repo's state, not to an external domain fact.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: rule 15 requires verifying an external/versioned fact before acting on it; rule 18 requires surfacing a contradiction between the prompt and the CODEBASE; neither explicitly obligates telling the owner they were wrong about something outside the codebase (Stripe, Swiss law, a library's real behavior) once the assistant has checked and found the owner's version false
findings.where_it_should_live: CLAUDE.md, as an explicit extension of rule 18's scope to external facts, or a new short rule adjacent to rule 15
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule; not mechanically gateable (no reliable way to detect 'owner asserted a false external fact' via regex) -- this is a judgment-class principle, not a gate candidate

findings.title: General technical jargon is unguarded; only estate-internal jargon is gated
findings.principle: A domain/technical term used in an owner-facing reply (race condition, idempotency key, webhook signature, RLS policy, CSRF, connection pool) is translated into plain words the first time it is used, the same discipline already applied to estate-internal terms (hook names, PreToolUse, orchestrator).
findings.why: The one live enforcement for jargon (concise-response-gate's JARGON regex) is scoped exclusively to this Claude Code estate's own vocabulary (PreToolUse, settings.json, matcher, subagents, orchestrator, worktrees, ledgers, precedence chain). A backend/security explanation full of general engineering jargon (race condition, idempotent, CSRF token, N+1 query) trips nothing, even though feedback_plain_english.md's 2026-06-08 addendum explicitly demands translating every technical term the moment it is used and gives this as a worked example: 'don't write "I gated getSession behind a session check"... say...'.
findings.local_evidence: hooks/concise-response-gate.py lines 122-130, the JARGON regex list is entirely estate-tooling nouns (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/settings.json/matcher/regex/state file/triaged/self-test/precedence chain/supersession/orchestrator/worktrees/ledgers/file:line) -- zero general engineering terms.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n "race condition|idempotent|CSRF|N+1|webhook signature" hooks/concise-response-gate.py -> zero. The behavioral rule exists only in memory/feedback_plain_english.md, no gate.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the estate-jargon half is gated (concise-response-gate JARGON regex, even though the gate's BLOCKING half is neutered per finding 4, the jargon check inside it uses stderr, not the neutered block path -- confirm this sub-check still fires); general technical jargon has zero coverage, gated or behavioral-only
findings.where_it_should_live: either extend concise-response-gate's JARGON list, or fold into a plain-language checklist item in REPORT_SYSTEM.md
findings.enforcement: gate: extend the existing JARGON regex in concise-response-gate.py with a general-engineering-terms list; low effort since the mechanism already exists, it just needs a bigger word list -- but note finding 4: the block path around this gate is currently neutered, so even a fixed regex list would only ever print, never enforce, unless the neutering is separately addressed

findings.title: No principle for reporting which verification depth actually ran, at the scale where the round-budget system exists
findings.principle: When a task went through the layered loop (rule 9 / LOOP_SYSTEM), the closing summary states how many review rounds it took and whether it converged clean or hit the 3-round escalation cap. This is a transparency-into-process report, not a cost-justification report, and must not be reframed as budget-consciousness.
findings.why: The estate already tiers verification depth by change size (rule 9's table: 0 rounds for a surgical fix, 2-3 rounds for a new route) and tiers models by task class (MODEL_ROUTING.md). None of that internal bookkeeping is required to surface to the owner, so there is no way for the owner to notice, from the report alone, that a task silently used fewer rounds than its own size class calls for (the failure that rule 9's own convergence rule is designed to catch INTERNALLY, but which the owner can't audit externally without re-deriving it from the transcript).
findings.why_scale_note: IMPORTANT: memory/feedback_optimize_for_best_not_cheap.md explicitly bans framing agent work as 'cheap'/'budget-conscious' -- any implementation of this finding must report depth as a PROCESS-INTEGRITY signal (did the loop run its own stated round budget) not as a cost/efficiency metric, or it contradicts that standing memory.
findings.local_evidence: LOOP_SYSTEM.md's round-budget table and MODEL_ROUTING's tiering exist and are read by the orchestrator every substantial task, but REPORT_SYSTEM.md's 5-item summary template (outcome/files/verified/parked/links) has no slot for 'rounds run' or 'model tier used'.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rln "tokens spent|context used|% context|effort spent" CLAUDE.md REPORT_SYSTEM.md hooks/*.py -> zero hits anywhere in the estate.
findings.where_it_should_live: REPORT_SYSTEM.md section 4, as an optional 6th line only for tasks that actually ran the layered loop (not every turn)
findings.enforcement: checklist; not gateable without conflicting with the neutered-gate lesson from finding 4 (another blocking gate risks the same double-send complaint) -- lowest priority of this batch, and only relevant once a task is complex enough to have gone through /refine at all

findings.title: Reviewer-disagreement handling exists only for multi-model council use, not the default single-reviewer loop
findings.principle: The default coder-then-loop-reviewer cycle (rule 13) uses exactly one reviewer voice per round. When a reviewer's PASS verdict conflicts with evidence the orchestrator itself already holds from earlier in the same task (a prior grep, an earlier failed check), the orchestrator states the conflict explicitly and re-checks before accepting PASS, rather than trusting the more recent verdict by default.
findings.why: FABLE_DNA pattern 14 ('report agreement vs disagreement explicitly; convergence = settled, divergence = a real fork for the owner') is the only estate text that names how to handle two verification sources disagreeing, and it is scoped explicitly to llm-council multi-model usage (a judgment-class, opt-in workflow), not to the everyday single coder/reviewer loop that rule 13 makes the DEFAULT for all substantial work. In the default loop there is exactly one reviewer, so nothing in the standing law says what the orchestrator should do if its OWN prior-turn observation (not another reviewer) conflicts with the reviewer's verdict -- rule 19 covers 'suspect an empty subagent result' but not 'suspect a non-empty but contradicted one'.
findings.local_evidence: FABLE_DNA.md line 28 (pattern 14) is filed under 'Gate 3, adversarial' and its encoding line says 'llm-council usage law; feedback_owner_literal_over_council' -- both council-specific. LOOP_SYSTEM.md's description of the reviewer ('read-only and adversarial... defaults to FAIL when it can't verify') never addresses what happens when the reviewer's PASS conflicts with something the orchestrator already knows.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn "disagree|divergence|conflicting verdict" LOOP_SYSTEM.md fable-execution/SKILL.md CLAUDE.md -> only the FABLE_DNA council-scoped hit above.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: fully covered for the opt-in multi-model council path; not covered for the default single-reviewer loop that rule 13 makes standard
findings.where_it_should_live: LOOP_SYSTEM.md, as an addendum to the reviewer description
findings.enforcement: behavioral rule for now; a gate would need to diff the orchestrator's own turn history against the reviewer's verdict, which is a meaningfully harder detection problem than the existing regex gates -- appropriate to defer until a real incident of this shape occurs (this finding is 'expect', reasoned from the pattern-library gap, not observed as a live bug)
